About Carolina Foods Carolina Foods LLC produces high-quality Duchess branded and private-label bakery goods for retail customers nationwide. Based in Pineville in the Charlotte, North Carolina area, our bakery brings product development and manufacturing together, giving leaders a direct connection to the products, people, and decisions that drive our business. Our people are central to our success. We value leaders who take pride in their work, share ideas, and build strong partnerships. Our commitment to safety, food safety and quality, operational excellence, and continuous improvement guides how we work and grow. Your Role As Head Of Engineering A hands-on engineering doer, not a program administrator. This role owns the plant's forward-looking improvement agenda, making existing lines better and building the capital pipeline that makes the plant fundamentally more capable and personally does the engineering work behind it: specs, FMEAs, business cases, and startup. It does not run day-to-day reactive maintenance or the plant's full legacy PM program. What it does own outright is the technical integrity of everything it touches: every project this person leads is engineered and commissioned to a real standard, not just installed and walked away from. Success looks like a live pipeline of improvement and capital projects, each with a credible business case, delivered on time and on budget, engineered to hold up, and with realized results tracked against what was promised. What This Role Is Not Not a day-to-day reactive maintenance role, floor-level PM execution and shift standards stay with the Maintenance Lead. Not, on its own, a rebuild of the plant's entire legacy PM program across every existing asset, that comprehensive lift is a future Engineering Lead's mandate once the plant adds that seat. This role's reliability and FMEA discipline applies fully and personally to everything it touches, its own projects and the assets it's asked to dig into, not to the full inherited asset base on day one. Key Responsibilities Continuous Improvement Pipeline (Existing Lines) Own the loss/opportunity Pareto for existing lines - OEE, yield, changeover time, rate, and labor productivity - and convert it into a prioritized improvement pipeline. Apply flow/constraint analysis (Theory of Constraints) to find the plant's true system constraint before proposing a fix, rather than optimizing a line in isolation. Lead structured improvement events (Kaizen/DMAIC) with cross-functional teams and put a control plan behind every completed improvement so gains are sustained and visible in the data months later. Capital Project Development, Design & Justification Own capital project scoping, specification, and the business case - ROI/payback, cross-functional alignment with Finance, Operations, and Quality, and the formal approval (AFE) package. Build and prioritize the capital project pipeline against the plant's strategic priorities, in partnership with the COO and plant leadership. Lead vendor/OEM selection, design review, and installation oversight personally - this role is the plant's technical authority on its own projects, not a project manager coordinating someone else's engineering. Commissioning, Reliability & Startup (Hands-On) Personally treat every project as complete only once a real commissioning package is delivered: performance validated against design intent, a failure mode and criticality analysis (FMEA) completed, PM procedures and frequencies derived from that FMEA, spare parts strategy defined, and operating parameters (rate limits, setpoints) validated against real flow data - never assumed from a single output point. Lead or directly support root cause analysis on failures tied to this role's own projects or the plant's highest-impact assets, in partnership with the Maintenance Lead; reject "replaced the part" as a root cause. Own the formal handoff of new or modified equipment to the Maintenance Lead, including training, documentation, and a defined transition point before moving to the next project. Track realized results against the original business case for at least two full quarters post-startup and report the gap openly. Required What Matters Most Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Process, or Manufacturing Engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience in a highly automated manufacturing environment. Track record personally leading capital projects from spec through startup - not just coordinating others' engineering - ideally in food or CPG manufacturing. Demonstrated continuous improvement leadership (Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent) with results tied to OEE, yield, or throughput gains. Working knowledge of FMEA, RCA methodology, and PM strategy development as engineering disciplines applied hands-on, not administered. Strong financial acumen - comfortable building and defending an ROI/payback case to Finance and executive leadership. Preferred Lean Six Sigma Black Belt. Experience with automated packaging/wrapping equipment and high-speed bakery or food production lines. Familiarity with capital appropriation (AFE) processes in a PE-backed or multi-site manufacturing environment. Familiarity with CMMS/EAM platforms (e.g., RedZone). Leadership Standards Does the engineering personally - specs, FMEAs, and validated parameters - rather than delegating the technical substance and managing only the schedule. Builds the business case on real data and conservative assumptions - never sells a project on a number that won't hold up under scrutiny. Protects the pipeline from becoming a firefighting queue; escalates instead of quietly absorbing reactive work that belongs elsewhere. Reports realized projectresults and technical limitations honestly, including projects that fell short. Skills For Success Hands-on engineering: Personally, develop specifications, technical analyses, FMEAs, and validated operating parameters and maintains ownership of the technical substance. Project and budget management: Integrates scope, schedule, resources, cost forecasts, vendor commitments, and risk controls to deliver approved projects. Financial and analytical judgment: Challenges assumptions, uses reliable operating data, and distinguishes projected benefits from verified results. Systems thinking and problem solving: Uses flow analysis, constraint analysis, and structured RCA to address causes and improve plant-wide performance. Influence and communication: Leads across functions without direct supervisory authority, explains technical tradeoffs clearly, and reports setbacks honestly. Execution and sustainability: Protects agreed priorities, documents decisions, trains operating owners, and follows results through commissioning, handoff, and sustained operation. Work Environment And Physical Demands Onsite role in a high-volume industrial bakery, combining plant-floor leadership with office work for planning, analysis, and project coordination. Requires walking and standing in production areas and accessing equipment areas for inspection and startup support. Conditions may include heat, noise, moving equipment, and material-handling traffic. Required personal protective equipment, hygiene practices, and safe-work procedures must be followed. Flexibility is needed for off-shift work, weekends, shutdowns, emergencies, and project-related travel Essential functions may be performed with reasonable accommodation. Come Join Us! Bring your engineering expertise, leadership, and passion for solving problems to Carolina Foods. Help build reliable bakery operations, develop strong technical teams, and turn investments into lasting results. If you enjoy hands-on leadership and working with senior leaders to improve performance, we invite you to apply or contact our Human Resources team.

One Team: We don’t think of ourselves as “Acquisition Marketers”, “Engineers”, “Data Analysts”, or “Product Managers”. Performance measures The following are proposed starting targets, not established EP results or certified industry benchmarks. Confirm baselines and definitions within 30 days and agree phased targets with the Site Leader and Finance. Apply the same service rules to external and interplant customers; show results separately. KPI Definition’s And Proposed Target Customer OTIF - Orders delivered on time and in full ÷ orders due, using the original agreed date and quantity. Target ≥100% monthly; record approved changes separately. Material availability - Production hours lost to unavailable required materials. Target zero preventable hours; log every event, cause and recovery. Schedule adherence - Work orders completed within the agreed window and quantity ÷ work orders due under the frozen schedule. Shared with Operations; target ≥95% weekly. Report changes separately. Inventory accuracy - Exact-match item/lot/location/quantity/status records ÷ records counted. Target ≥99.5% monthly and 100% for designated critical stock; also report gross absolute value variance. Inventory investment - Days of inventory = average inventory at cost ÷ trailing 90-day daily cost of goods sold. Proposed 12-month goal: reduce 10% from approved baseline without service loss; track aged stock separately. Supplier delivery - Purchase-order lines received by the agreed required date and in full ÷ lines due. Target ≥98% monthly; no retrospective date changes to improve results. Transaction timeliness - Receipts and transfers posted within 24 hours; completed work orders accurately closed within 24 hours of final required sign-off. Target ≥95% for each; 100% by Finance close cutoff. Supply chain cost - Controllable spend within approved volume-adjusted budget. Proposed six-month goal: reduce avoidable premium freight 50% from the first 90-day baseline; Finance validates realized savings. Flexibility in scheduling is required to support training across multiple shifts, including early morning, evening, or off-shift hours as needed. Ensure technical content is reviewed and approved by the appropriate content owners. Coordinate structured cross-training to improve workforce flexibility and coverage of critical positions; work with supervisors to establish individual training and development plans. Coordinate training for new equipment and new or revised manufacturing processes before employees begin affected work. Provide refresher or remedial training when performance issues, quality concerns, safety incidents, process deviations, or procedure changes identify training needs. Maintain a strong floor presence, observe assigned tasks, coach employees, and serve as an approachable resource for manufacturing process and work requirement questions. Immediately communicate unsafe practices, quality risks, or significant deviations from standard work to the appropriate supervisor or manager. Conduct or coordinate practical skill assessments and document demonstrated competency before recommending employees for independent work; coordinate qualification approval with production management and designated technical owners. Maintain accurate employee training records, skills matrices, qualification matrices, and cross-training matrices; track required training, completion, demonstrated competency, and renewal requirements. Monitor upcoming and overdue training or qualifications, communicate skill gaps to supervisors, and follow through on completion plans. Keep training records current and available for internal, customer, or regulatory audits; protect employee information and follow record-retention and access requirements. Provide regular management updates on training completion, qualification status, skill coverage, and training effectiveness; participate in production, safety, quality, and employee development meetings. Demonstrated experience in training, coaching, mentoring, or leading manufacturing employees in roles such as Manufacturing Trainer, Training Coordinator, Lead Operator, Team Leader or Production Lead. Demonstrated experience in developing and maintaining training matrices, qualification systems, visual work instructions, one-point lessons, or structured on-the-job training programs. Working knowledge of safety, quality, and production practices. Ability to read and understand work instructions, SOPs, drawings, specifications, and other documentation applicable to assigned operations. Ability to demonstrate manufacturing processes clearly and provide constructive coaching and feedback. Strong verbal and written communication, organizational, recordkeeping, and follow-up skills. Summary: The Director of Manufacturing Operations is the senior manufacturing operations leader for the Denton, Texas campus. Plant 1 performs final assembly of make-to-order precision cooling units. We are looking for a hands-on, visible leader who turns strategy into measurable results on the shop floor and builds a team that can sustain them. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Safety, People & Culture Build and lead a capable site leadership team; hire, onboard, coach, and evaluate managers, and develop succession depth for key roles. Set clear expectations and hold people accountable fairly and consistently, applying company policy (attendance, conduct, corrective action) in partnership with HR. Create a respectful, engaged workplace where concerns are raised early and problems are solved at the lowest effective level. Own site safety performance; drive hazard and near-miss reporting, root cause analysis, and timely closure of corrective actions. Production & Delivery Deliver the annual production and revenue plan for the Denton campus, meeting customer commitments for on-time delivery and quality. Manage capacity, staffing, and shift structure across both plants to support growth with the right headcount and overhead structure. Synchronize Plant 2 component output with Plant 1 assembly demand so internal supply supports, rather than constrains, final assembly. Planning, Materials & Warehouse Lead site planning, scheduling, receiving, warehousing, material handling, and inventory management to secure material availability, reduce lead times, and prevent shortages and stock-outs. Partner with corporate Supply Planning and Procurement on SAP master data, MRP, and supplier performance; assist with procurement guidance when needed (dotted line). Ensure supply chain policies and procedures are followed, and drive inventory accuracy and inventory turns targets. Maintenance & Manufacturing Engineering Lead preventive and predictive maintenance programs to improve equipment uptime, with a focus on automated and capital-intensive equipment at Plant 2. Direct Manufacturing Engineering on process design, standard work, line balancing, work instructions, and new product introduction handoffs. Lead installation, commissioning, and acceptance (FAT/SAT) of capital equipment, and build and justify site capital plans. Plant 2 Start-Up & Site Integration Lead Plant 2 through start-up and ramp-up to stable, rate-capable production, working with PMO and cross-functional partners on schedule, readiness, and staffing. Merge Plant 1 and Plant 2 into a single site organization with common roles, processes, meetings, and reporting. Operating System, Performance & Continuous Improvement Deploy the STULZ Manufacturing Operating Model at the site: tiered daily meetings (Tier 1-3), a weekly site staff meeting, standard KPIs, and visual management. Translate annual strategy deployment (Hoshin Kanri / X-matrix) into site objectives, owners, and action plans, and review progress monthly. Lead a continuous improvement culture using Lean tools (5S, standard work, kaizen, problem solving); share best practices with other STULZ plants and adopt theirs. Support senior leadership in long- and short-range planning, policies, and objectives for U.S. manufacturing. Measurable improvement in safety, on-time delivery, productivity, and inventory accuracy versus baseline. Strong analytical skills, including data analysis and trending in Excel; Power BI or similar is a plus. Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, bills of material, and specifications. Preferred Experience leading a greenfield plant start-up, major expansion, or integration of multiple facilities. Exposure to fabrication and finishing processes (sheet metal, welding/brazing, powder coating) and to automated equipment. Experience with ISO 9001 quality systems. Experience in the data center, HVAC, or mission-critical equipment industry. Education/Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations/Supply Chain Management, Business, or a related field and 10+ years of manufacturing experience; Master’s degree or MBA a plus. 7+ years managing managers in a manufacturing environment, including multi-department or multi-shift responsibility. Summary The Senior Maintenance Manager is the plant reliability leader and the daily execution owner for maintenance at the Fall River food manufacturing facility. This role balances strategic asset-management leadership with strong floor presence. The successful leader will establish a CMMS-centered system for work identification, prioritization, planning, scheduling, execution, closeout, analysis, and continuous improvement while personally engaging in daily production readiness, breakdown response, shift support, and cross-functional problem solving. This is not a primarily administrative position and not a permanent “chief troubleshooter” role. The position is accountable for building a capable team and a repeatable reliability system that reduces recurring failures, improves planning work execution, protects food safety and employee safety, and increases productive pounds per scheduled day. Essential Duties Daily operating involvement (35% – 45%) Visible on the floor; leads morning review; supports urgent failures; verifies startup and post-repair readiness; removes execution barriers. CMMS planning and execution (25% – 35%) Approved work is prioritized, planned, scheduled, kitted, executed, closed with quality data, and reviewed for backlog and repeat failure. Reliability strategy and improvement (20% – 25%) Top assets have reliability plans; PM/Pd.M. tasks are optimized; RCAs lead to permanent changes; risk and capital plans are current. People and capability (10% – 15%) Shift coverage, technical skills, controls/electrical depth, vendor knowledge transfer, and supervisor standard work improve measurably. CMMS Governance and Work Management Own the plant maintenance workflow from notification through technical closeout, including request screening, priority assignment, approval, planning, scheduling, execution, completion, failure coding, labor and material capture, and effectiveness follow-up. Establish and enforce work-order standards: clear problem statement, asset hierarchy, failure mode, production impact, safety and food-safety risk, craft requirements, estimated hours, parts, parts, parts, parts, permits, procedures, post-work checks, and closeout comments. Lead weekly scheduling with Operations, Planning, Sanitation, FSQA and Engineering. Maintain a frozen weekly schedule with an agreed emergency-work rule and visible plan-versus-actual review. Build and manage a risk-based backlog using asset criticality, production loss, safety, food safety, recurrence, labor availability, parts status, and shutdown-window requirements. Develop dashboards for PM compliance, schedule compliance, planned-work percentage, emergency work, backlog age, work-order completion, wrench-time barriers, repeat failure, MTBF, MTTR, downtime, and data completeness. Ensure CMMS is the system of record for equipment history, BOMs, job plans, procedures, technical documents, vendor reports, calibration records, critical spares, warranties, and recurring work. Daily Plant Execution and Floor Leadership Conduct an early-morning review of overnight events, staffing, open failures, PM results, startup readiness, safety concerns, food-safety risks, parts constraints, and the daily production plan. Maintain visible floor presence across shifts, particularly during startup, changeovers, critical maintenance, chiller or filler recovery, high-speed-line operation, and post-repair validation. Assign a single accountable maintenance owner to each plant-critical event and ensure containment, recovery, permanent corrective action, and verification are clearly separated. Coordinate response to equipment failures without allowing emergency work to consume the planned schedule unchecked. Escalate resource conflicts and protect the highest-value work. Require production-like testing after major maintenance, including correct product or test conditions, operating speed, upstream/downstream interfaces, controls, safety devices, quality checks, and operator acceptance. Provide daily and weekly updates that show what failed, business impact, current containment, next action, owner, due date, parts or support needed, and evidence required for closure. Reliability Engineering and Chronic Loss Elimination Build asset-level reliability plans for the plant’s top recurring losses, initially emphasizing critical chillers, fillers, demisters, film and seal systems, Douglas, Hartness, Clicklock, lidded, MVC, X-ray, palletizers, printers and labeling systems. Use downtime, work-order, condition-monitoring, quality, hold, waste, and production data to identify bad actors and rank work by lost pounds, risk, recurrence, repair cost, lead time, and capacity impact. Lead structured RCA for significant and repeat failures. Convert findings into updated PMs, Pd.M. routes, operator care, job plans, spares, training, design correction, controls changes, and operating standards. Develop condition-based maintenance where technically and financially justified, including vibration, oil analysis, thermography, temperature trends, alignment, belt or chain wear, lubrication, electrical condition, and health controls. Partner with Engineering on design corrections, obsolescence, lifecycle risk, equipment upgrades, control reliability, sanitation-compatible design, and multi-year asset replacement strategy. Preventive and Predictive Maintenance Optimize PM frequency and task content using failure history, OEM requirements, criticality, operating context, inspection findings, mean time to failure, and technician feedback rather than calendar frequency alone. Create standard job plans with labor, duration, safety steps, tools, parts, photos or drawings, acceptance criteria, and documented post-maintenance validation. Coordinate rotating maintenance windows with Planning, Operations and Sanitation and publish a weekly, monthly and quarterly shutdown calendar. Audit PM quality in the field. Completion is not accepted solely as a transaction; required condition findings, measurements, parts used, and abnormalities must be documented. Ensure calibration and inspection programs for critical devices are risk-based, documented, scheduled, and aligned with FSQA requirements. Team Leadership and Capability Development Lead supervisors, planners, technicians, electricians, controls resources, utilities or refrigeration support, and contractors with clear roles, daily direction, standard work, coaching, and accountability. Complete a shift-by-shift skills matrix covering mechanical, electrical, controls, utilities, refrigeration, filling, sealing, coding, packaging, troubleshooting, LOTO, food safety, and CMMS capabilities. Build qualification plans and cross-training to reduce single-point knowledge risk, especially for off-shift response, high-speed packaging, fillers, chillers, controls, PLCs, printers and critical process equipment. Use OEM and cross-site support for hands-on knowledge transfer, requiring internal employees to participate, document learning, and demonstrate capability after vendor work. Create a staffing and on-call model that supports the operating schedule without overreliance on a small number of individuals or repetitive weekend coverage. Spare Parts, Vendors and Cost Control Establish asset BOMs and critical-spares levels using failure history, criticality, lead time, shelf life, redundancy, repairability, installed base, and financial exposure. Classify parts as stock, insurance spare, repairable, vendor-held, or order-on-demand and maintain min/max, reorder, cycle-count, and obsolete-parts controls. Manage OEM and contractor performance using defined scope, pre-work data, parts readiness, plant escorts, acceptance criteria, service reports, action closure, and knowledge transfer. Build and manage maintenance operating and capital budgets; review repair-versus-replace decisions; obtain competitive bids; track labor, parts, contractor, downtime, and avoided-loss value. Education and/or Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Industrial Technology, Maintenance Management or a related field, technical or trade-school credential with substantial relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Eight or more years of progressive maintenance, reliability or engineering experience in a 24/7 manufacturing environment, including significant people-leadership responsibility. Demonstrated ownership of a CMMS/EAM work-management system, including asset hierarchy, work-order workflow, PMs, planning and scheduling, failure coding, backlog, materials and reporting. Experience leading maintenance in food, beverage, dairy, pharmaceutical, CPG or another regulated manufacturing environment. Strong mechanical, electrical and controls troubleshooting literacy with the ability to lead technical teams across fillers, conveyors, packaging, pumps, motors, gearboxes, pneumatics, hydraulics, instrumentation and PLC-controlled systems. Experience applying RCA, PM optimization, condition-based maintenance, spare-parts criticality, contractor management, budgeting and capital planning. Preferred CMRP, CRL, PMP, PE, electrician, refrigeration, controls or related professional certification. Experience with high-speed food packaging, spiral chilling or freezing, aseptic or hygienic process equipment, refrigeration and utility systems, coding and labeling, and sanitary design. Experience implementing or materially improving CMMS use, planner/scheduler effectiveness, storeroom controls, PdM routes and reliability dashboards. Lean, TPM, RCM, FMEA, A3, 5-Why, Six Sigma or similar continuous-improvement experience. The playbook is written, the systems are in place, and the scorecards exist. What separates a good month from a great one is whether every brand actually runs the process the same way, every day - and whether anyone is watching closely enough to know. The Operations Support Manager is that person. Reporting to the Vice President of Operations / Chief Operating Officer, this role turns the data our field and call center operations generate into clear, usable reporting, then uses that reporting to hold brands accountable to the ACS standard. The role sits at the intersection of analysis and execution: build the report, read what it says, and go make sure the brand does something about it. The work covers four things - operational reporting and analysis, call center performance, process compliance across brands, and follow-up on outstanding replacement proposals. The right person is analytical and detail-oriented, but is not content to email a report and move on. What This Role Owns 1. Reporting and analysis. Build and maintain the recurring reporting that shows how every brand is actually performing, and keep the underlying data clean. 2. Call center performance. Keep the call boards full and the centers efficient, and push outbound effort when inbound demand will not carry the budget. 3. Process compliance. Verify that every brand runs the ACS process the ACS way, and prove it with data rather than assumptions. 4. Proposal follow-up. Own the outstanding proposal report, make sure unsold estimates are being worked, and re-engage the ones that are not. Essential Duties and ResponsibilitiesReporting and Data Analysis Build, maintain, and distribute the recurring daily, weekly, and monthly reporting out of ServiceTitan: call volume, booking rates, dispatch efficiency, technician performance, revenue, membership, and the estimate and proposal pipeline. Analyze operational and sales data across the call center and field operations to identify trends, bottlenecks, and opportunities, and bring the findings to the Vice President of Operations with a recommendation attached. Partner with leadership to define and track the KPIs on the platform scorecard, and keep KPI definitions and rollup logic consistent across all 14 brands so the numbers compare apples to apples. Audit the data entered into ServiceTitan for accuracy and completeness - job types, lead source attribution, tagging, and job costing - and drive corrections at the source rather than patching them in the report. Call Center Performance and Board Fill Monitor call center performance across the platform: speed to answer, abandoned call rate, booking rate, average handle time, first-call resolution, and conversion by customer service representative. Watch the call board daily. Know how many service calls each brand has booked against capacity, how far out the board is scheduled, and where the holes are before the day starts. Tie board fill to the revenue budget. Know what a brand needs on the board this week to hit its number, and raise the alarm early when the math does not work. Drive outbound effort when inbound demand will not fill the board - maintenance agreements due, unsold estimates, recall and deferred repair lists, membership renewals, and dormant customer campaigns. Document and continuously refine call center standard operating procedures: booking protocols, call scripts, escalation paths, and quality standards. Monitor call recordings and quality scoring to identify coaching opportunities and process gaps, and work with call center leadership to close them. Help train new and existing call center staff on ServiceTitan workflows and best-practice standards. Process Compliance Across Brands Maintain and communicate the ACS standard operating procedures for the core operating functions: call taking and booking, dispatch and scheduling, technician workflow, estimate presentation and follow-up, install handoff, quality control, warranty and callback handling, and job closeout. Support the plumbing expansion with process build-out, reporting, and follow-up discipline for the new service line. Verify that brands are working their unsold estimates to the ACS standard. Audit ServiceTitan for logged follow-up activity - not just whether an estimate closed, but whether anyone touched it and when. Report on pipeline health - aged proposal dollars, touch rate, recovery rate, and close rate by brand and by seller - and escalate brands that consistently leave estimates unworked. Keep lead source attribution accurate in ServiceTitan so campaign performance and cost per acquired customer can be trusted. Monitor and report the conversion chain end to end - lead to booked call, booked to run, run to estimate presented, estimate to sold - and flag where it is breaking. Hold brands accountable for answering the phone, booking the call, running the appointment, and following up on marketing-generated demand. Learn the platform and the reporting. Visit the call centers and the largest brands. Produce a written baseline of where each brand stands on call board fill, process adherence, and proposal follow-up. Days 45-120. Get the recurring report package stable and trusted. Stand up the outstanding proposal audit and daily board-fill visibility for every brand. Publish the first process compliance scorecard. Days 120-240. Accepts nothing on the strength of a verbal assurance and always goes back to the data. Analyst and operator both. Notices that a brand has been miscoding lead sources, or that a seller has not touched an estimate in 21 days, before anyone else does. Influence without authority. Gets a veteran General Manager to change a practice by being useful and being right, not by escalating. Direct and respectful. Delivers uncomfortable feedback early, plainly, and without drama. Self-directed. Prioritizes competing reporting deadlines and follow-up queues without being managed through them. Occasional exposure to shops, warehouses, and job sites during brand visits. This is a highly visible executive leadership role for an experienced manufacturing leader who can successfully balance strategy, execution, people leadership, and operational discipline. The Vice President of Operations will be responsible for strengthening operational performance, developing high-performing teams, improving processes and systems, and creating a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, safety, and respect. Develop and execute operational strategies aligned with business objectives, customer requirements, financial goals, and growth plans. Establish, strengthen, and standardize operating procedures, processes, systems, and performance expectations. Drive a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence. Use operational data and performance metrics to identify opportunities and sustain measurable improvements. Establish key performance indicators and maintain accountability for operational results. Evaluate manufacturing processes, workflows, equipment, and organizational structure to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Champion a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with applicable environmental, health, safety, and regulatory requirements. Build, coach, develop, and retain a high-performing operations leadership team. Foster a workplace culture grounded in respect, collaboration, integrity, and trust. Partner cross-functionally with Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, Human Resources, Sales, and other business functions. Support capital planning, equipment investments, plant improvements, and long-term capacity planning. Identify operational risks and develop practical solutions that support both immediate business needs and long-term sustainability. Significant progressive leadership experience within manufacturing operations. Senior-level responsibility for plant operations or multi-functional manufacturing operations strongly preferred. Demonstrated success leading complex manufacturing organizations and improving operational performance. Metals industry experience strongly preferred, including experience within copper, steel, aluminum, casting, foundry, rolling, fabrication, or related manufacturing environments. Strong technical understanding of manufacturing processes, equipment, maintenance, production systems, quality, and process improvement. Proven experience developing and implementing standard operating procedures, operational systems, and process improvements. Demonstrated ability to lead both strategically and tactically. Proven ability to translate business objectives into executable operational plans. Experience building, developing, and retaining high-performing teams. Strong understanding of operational KPIs, cost management, productivity, quality, capacity, and continuous improvement. Ability to lead effectively in a hands-on manufacturing environment and build credibility with employees at all levels. Strong communication, decision-making, problem-solving, and change-management skills. Demonstrated leadership style rooted in accountability, collaboration, integrity, and respect. Hold teams accountable while providing the support needed to succeed. Challenge existing processes thoughtfully and constructively. Develop leaders and build stronger teams. Demonstrate a continuous improvement mindset. Balance immediate operational needs with long-term strategic priorities. Lead with integrity, consistency, and respect. Job Description Job Description Company Sabrosura Foods is one of the leading marketers of Hispanic products sold throughout the U.S. under the well-known brand names of Pancho’s, El Viajero, Reynaldo’s and La Morenita. We are dedicated to delivering authentic and high-quality products to our customers. Our passion lies in creating delicious, culturally inspired foods that connect people and cultures. Our drive for quality, authenticity, and innovation compels us to deliver exceptional products that celebrate the diverse cultures and tastes of our customers. Job Summary As the Operations Manager for our food manufacturing plants, you are responsible for leading and optimizing day-to-day operational activities within both of the manufacturing facilities to ensure the safe, efficient, and cost-effective production, storage, and movement of products. Reporting directly to the Plant Manager, this position provides leadership across Production and Warehouse operations and provides day-to-day operational direction to the Logistics Coordinator. The Operations Manager works closely with the Logistics Director, Maintenance, Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Human Resources, and other cross-functional teams to achieve plant performance objectives. The Operations Manager has primary responsibility for production execution, warehouse operations, operational flow, and oversight of logistics coordination and third-party logistics (3PL) activities. This position will drive continuous improvement initiatives, improve labor and equipment utilization, reduce waste and operating costs, and establish a culture of accountability, safety, teamwork, and operational excellence. The Operations Manager serves as a key partner to the Plant Manager in the daily management of the facilities and is accountable for ensuring effective coordination and flow between production, warehouse, inventory, and logistics activities. Job Responsibilities Operations & Production Leadership Provide operational leadership across two manufacturing plants, supporting daily production activities while driving safety, compliance, and operational excellence. Lead daily Production and Warehouse operations to ensure production plans, inventory requirements, and customer orders are executed safely, efficiently, and on schedule. Provide direction, coaching, and accountability to Production Supervisors, Leads, and the Warehouse Supervisor. Establish operational priorities based on production schedules, business needs, inventory requirements, and customer demand. Monitor production performance, labor utilization, overtime, yields, waste, downtime, and other key metrics; implement corrective actions as needed. Maintain a strong presence on the production floor and in the warehouse to identify bottlenecks, resolve issues, and support frontline leadership. Partner with Human Resources and operational leadership on staffing, workforce planning, employee relations, and performance management. Warehouse, Logistics & 3PL Provide leadership and direction to the Warehouse Supervisor to ensure efficient warehouse operations, inventory control, material flow, staging, and loading. Ensure effective coordination between Production, Warehouse, and Logistics to support production schedules, finished-goods availability, and customer requirements. Directly supervise and provide day-to-day operational direction to the Logistics Coordinator and ensure effective communication between Production, Warehouse, Sales, drivers, and other stakeholders. Partner with the Logistics Coordinator to resolve delivery, scheduling, transportation, and customer-service issues that impact plant operations. Support the management and performance of third-party logistics (3PL) providers by monitoring service performance, addressing operational issues, and identifying improvement opportunities. Partner with the Logistics Director to align plant-level logistics activities with company-wide logistics strategies, policies, and initiatives. Process Improvement & Operational Excellence Lead and support continuous improvement initiatives to increase productivity, improve process flow, reduce waste, minimize downtime, and lower operating costs. Utilize Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, root cause analysis, and other continuous improvement methodologies as appropriate. Identify and implement process improvements across Production, Warehouse, Logistics, and other operational areas. Analyze operational data and KPIs to identify trends, recurring issues, and opportunities for improvement; ensure corrective actions are implemented and sustained. Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and operational excellence. Maintenance & Equipment Reliability Maintain a strong partnership with the Maintenance Supervisor to support equipment reliability, production uptime, and timely resolution of equipment-related issues. Collaborate with the Maintenance supervisor to prioritize repairs, preventive maintenance, reliability initiatives, and equipment improvements based on operational needs. Participate in root cause analysis of recurring equipment failures and support initiatives to reduce downtime and improve equipment reliability. Quality, Safety & Compliance Promote compliance with all applicable food safety, quality, safety, and regulatory requirements, including GMPs, HACCP, SQF, FDA, USDA, OSHA, and company policies. Partner with Quality Assurance to address quality issues, investigate deviations, and implement corrective and preventive actions. Promote a safe work environment by identifying hazards, participating in incident investigations, supporting safety programs, and ensuring corrective actions are completed. Foster a culture in which food safety, product quality, and employee safety are shared operational responsibilities. Performance, Cost & People Management Establish and monitor key operational performance indicators, including production efficiency, labor productivity, overtime, yield, waste, downtime, OEE, schedule attainment, inventory accuracy, on-time performance, safety, quality, and operating costs. Analyze operational performance and develop action plans to address gaps and improve results. Support the Plant Manager in managing operational costs, budgeting, forecasting, labor, overtime, material usage, waste, warehouse, and logistics expenses. Provide leadership, coaching, and development to frontline leaders; establish clear expectations and hold teams accountable for performance. Build a high-performing operational team through effective communication, coaching, employee engagement, and continuous learning. Cross-Functional Leadership Serve as the primary local point of coordination between Production, Warehouse, and Logistics to support efficient end-to-end operational flow. Work closely with the Plant Manager, Maintenance, Quality Assurance, Logistics, Supply Chain, Human Resources, Finance, Purchasing, and other functions to achieve plant objectives.

The Lasko Manager, Field Quality is responsible for Lasko’s product quality performance after products reach the consumer. This position owns the field quality data across all Lasko brands, sets the thresholds that trigger an investigation, leads each investigation to a verified corrective action on a defined schedule, and supplies field failure data to engineering, product integrity, and supplier quality for use in design and process decisions. This is an on-site position with travel to Lasko manufacturing and distribution sites and to suppliers. Primary location West Chester, PA headquarters. Candidates in Greater Boston / Burlington, MA will also be considered. Essential Functions Field Quality Monitoring and Early Detection Own the field quality data across all Lasko brands: Return rate and retailer defective return data Warranty claims Consumer service contacts Consumer ratings and review content Plant and supplier quality data as it bears on field performance Set and maintain the thresholds at which a change in the data opens an investigation, and revise them as product mix and sourcing change. Report field quality performance, open issues, owners, and due dates at the ELT quality review. Investigation and Closure Lead cross-functional investigations to closure, assigning an owner and a date for each action across engineering, supplier quality, plant quality, and consumer services. Chair the corrective and preventive action (CAPA) review, and hold each open item to its committed date. Apply structured problem-solving methods and hold the participating functions to them: 8D 5-Why Fishbone (cause and effect) Fault tree analysis DMAIC A3 Recommend containment actions, including stop ship, product hold, rework, and retailer notification, and present the evidence supporting the recommendation. Verify the effectiveness of each corrective action against post-implementation data before closing it. Escalate any issue involving product safety or regulatory compliance immediately on identification. Design and Supplier Feedback Supply field failure history to product integrity for use in DFMEA, and confirm that the failure modes seen in the field are represented. Issue supplier corrective action requests (SCARs) arising from field failures, and verify supplier responses against subsequent field data. Report the cost of poor quality attributable to field failures, and prioritize work against it. Standards and Development Define the standard for failure analysis documentation, investigation records, and corrective action closure, and apply it across the quality organization. Provide technical direction and coaching to Quality Assurance Engineers. Competencies And Abilities Ability to lead a cross-functional investigation in which no participant reports to this position. Ability to make a containment recommendation on incomplete information, and to state what is established and what is not. Ability to apply and teach structured problem-solving methods (8D, 5-Why, fishbone, fault tree, DMAIC, A3). Proficiency in statistical analysis and the interpretation of failure rate data (Excel, Minitab, or similar). Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, specifications, DFMEAs, PFMEAs, and control plans. Ability to present quality performance and issue status to an executive audience. Working knowledge of consumer product construction, including motors, heating elements, controls, and molded plastic components. Certifications And Special Requirements Working knowledge of ISO 9001 quality management system requirements. Working knowledge of core quality tools: FMEA, control plans, SPC, CAPA, and PPAP. Required/Desired Education And Experience Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, or related technical field required. 6 or more years of experience in product or manufacturing quality required. At least 2 years leading cross-functional corrective action to closure required. Experience in consumer products, appliances, or another high-volume consumer durable category preferred. Experience with warranty, returns, or field failure data preferred. Role Overview The Fire Sprinkler Operations / Service Manager is responsible for the day-to-day leadership and operational performance of the Fire Sprinkler Department , including inspections, service, repairs, and installations. The primary responsibility of this position is to ensure field technicians are properly scheduled, prepared, supported, and held accountable for completing work safely, efficiently, and professionally. They are responsible for ensuring technicians understand their assignments and have properly reviewed their materials, equipment, and job requirements before scheduled work. Job Readiness – Identify manpower, material, equipment, access, and coordination needs before work begins. Quality & Compliance – Maintain standards for workmanship, inspections, documentation, safety, and code compliance. Sales Coordination – Help resolve scope questions and prevent disconnects between what was sold and what is expected in the field. Interdepartmental Coordination – Work with Fire Alarm and other department leaders when projects require multiple disciplines. Customer Service – Address customer concerns, complaints, scheduling issues, and scope questions through resolution. Workload Management – Maintain awareness of department scheduling, backlog, staffing needs, and operational priorities. Management Communication – Meet regularly with the General Manager and communicate significant personnel, customer, staffing, and operational concerns. Required Qualifications NICET Level II certification in the applicable sprinkler discipline. Current applicable Virginia DPOR certification . Strong commercial fire sprinkler inspection, service, repair, and installation knowledge. Strong leadership, organization, delegation, communication, and customer service skills. Ability to prioritize competing responsibilities and remain productive and professional under pressure. Overall Expectation The manager is expected to take ownership of the daily operation of the sprinkler department . Success means technicians are prepared and supported, work is properly coordinated, customers receive professional service, departments communicate effectively, and problems are addressed before they become larger issues.

Tire Manager Classification Exempt Job Summary The Tire Operations Manager (TOM) will lead the tire service operations for our Houston Doggett Toyota Lift branch. This role is responsible for overseeing day-to-day performance, profitability, customer satisfaction, safety compliance, and operational efficiency across all tire-related functions. This leader will manage a dedicated team of tire technicians and support staff, oversee field service and shop scheduling, and maintain control of inventory, procurement, and equipment uptime. Financial & Operational Oversight Own and manage full departmental Profit & Loss (P&L) responsibilities. Develop and monitor operational budgets and forecasts. Foundry work is tough. It takes grit, it takes hard work, and it takes people who can think on their feet and solve complex problems. Are you up to the task? Our history dates back to 1905, when we began to produce castings in Elyria, Ohio, for the machine tool, gas engine and other industries. Our Hodge Foundry location began operation in 1876 and built a reputation for quality casting from its Greenville, Pennsylvania location. The two foundries joined to form a single company in 2008, which is today known as Elyria Foundry. We are a fast-paced, technically advanced, customer-focused operation creating high-quality, American-made products and we’re looking for individuals who are eager to learn and contribute to the Team! Position: Process Engineering Manager Summary: Plans, coordinates, and directs activities concerned with developing, maintaining, and optimizing foundry manufacturing processes. Maintains and develops standard operating procedures for all molding and core making manufacturing methods. Effectively problem solves and supports activities to drive continuous improvement. Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities: Develops, implements, and coordinates process control programs to prevent or eliminate defects in new or existing products by performing the following duties personally or through subordinate supervisors/staff: Analyzes, evaluates, and presents information concerning factors such as business situations, production capabilities, manufacturing problems, economic trends, and design and development of new products for consideration by other members of management team. Suggests and debates alternative methods and procedures to resolve internal and external root cause(s) of scrap Cooperates with other top management personnel in formulating and establishing company policies, operating procedures, and goals. Develops initial and subsequent modifications of process control program to delineate areas of responsibility, personnel requirements, and operational procedures within program. Reviews technical problems and procedures of departments and recommends solutions to problems or changes in procedures. Leads process engineering team within the organization. Keeps management team informed of significant issues or developments identified with current manufacturing methods and actions being taken to support improvement Designs and implement process training programs for key personnel in conjunction with managers. Investigates customer complaints regarding quality and maintains related database. Directs process engineering team engaged in process improvement/optimization activities Supports product engineering team in the analysis, inspection, design, test, and/or integration to assure product quality. Prepares and maintains control plans and revises/audits floor processes, responds to customers’ quality concerns Lead root cause analysis such as 8D and effective resolutions. Performs process engineering reviews of design documentation for compliance with stated requirements, including vendor quality manuals and company quality records. Applies statistical process control (SPC) and SQC methods for analyzing data to evaluate the current process and process changes. Documents data obtained during all process engineering activities, consistent with company policies and procedures. Develops new approaches to solve problems identified during manufacturing process audits Communicates significant issues or developments identified during process audits and provides recommended process improvements to management. Prepares reports to communicate involvement and results of process improvement activities Develops and initiates standards and methods for inspection, testing, and evaluation. Devises sampling procedures and designs and develops forms and instructions for recording, evaluating, and reporting quality and reliability data. Maintains a working knowledge of government and industry quality assurance standards. Supervisory Responsibilities: Manages a staff of process engineers and process engineering technicians. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of these subordinates. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems. Reasoning Ability: Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form. Education and/or Experience: Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of ten years’ related experience. Sand molding foundry experience required OR related experience Other Skills and Abilities: Ability to maintain, document and report objective evaluation of product quality Excellent organizational skills required to maintain detailed documentation and filing of quality records Intermediate to advanced skills in Microsoft Office Ability to mentor and teach at all levels in the organization Strong project management experience Ability to work off hours as needed Excellent written and verbal communication skills Ability to conduct root cause analysis and determine effective resolutions Ability to present data in effective formats to management, customers, vendors and plant personnel Strong problem-solving techniques Ability to perform SPC and SQC Physical Demands: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to sit. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms and climb or balance. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
